query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Earlier studies of other self-lubricating material systems reported low coefficients of friction at 704 °C and favorable friction and wear behavior over broad temperature ranges. However, these results do not resolve the limited understanding of wide-temperature tribological performance in CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys, and effectiveness must be maintained as operating temperature, load, and environment vary. Formulate one hypothesis that identifies a single intervention without presupposing its class, explains its mechanism, predicts friction and wear relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, defines its temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, relates it to prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled boron doping in the CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy will in situ generate nano-scale boride precipitates that, upon sliding at elevated temperatures, oxidize into a stable lubricious tribofilm. This intervention is expected to lower the coefficient of friction and wear rate across the full temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C compared to the undoped alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy matrix without any secondary phase or dopants.
generation.intervention: Incorporate a modest, controlled level of boron (e.g., approximately 5 vol%) during alloy synthesis to produce nano-scale boride precipitates within the matrix.
generation.conditions: Sliding tribological testing conducted over a temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C, under moderate to high loads, and in an environment where the oxygen partial pressure enables controlled oxidation.
generation.structural_mediator: Nano-scale boride precipitates that evolve into a lubricious oxide tribofilm during sliding at elevated temperatures.
generation.mechanism: At lower temperatures, the presence of boride precipitates improves the mechanical stability of the CoCrFeNi matrix, while at elevated temperatures the borides undergo controlled oxidation to form a thin, continuous lubricious tribofilm. This film reduces adhesion and friction and protects the underlying material from excessive wear, thereby stabilizing tribological performance over a broad temperature range.
generation.predicted_outcome: The boron-doped alloy will exhibit a consistently lower steady-state coefficient of friction and reduced wear rate compared to the undoped CoCrFeNi matrix, particularly noticeable at elevated temperatures (approaching 800 °C) and confirmed by improvements at temperatures around 704 °C as seen in related self-lubricating systems.
generation.baseline: The pristine CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy without the boron doping.
generation.boundary: This enhanced tribological performance is expected under conditions of moderate load and controlled oxygen exposure. Extreme loads, uncontrolled oxidizing environments, or very rapid temperature changes may disrupt the formation or stability of the lubricious film.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty about the precise kinetics and stability of the boride oxidation process under varying sliding speeds and load conditions, as well as the optimal boron concentration needed to balance low-temperature mechanical integrity and high-temperature lubrication.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of standard CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy and a second set doped with approximately 5 vol% boron. Subject both sets to sliding tribological tests using a pin-on-disk apparatus over a temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C, under identical moderate to high loads and in a controlled atmosphere that allows regulated oxidation. Record friction coefficient and wear rate continuously.
measurements: Coefficient of friction as a function of temperature
Wear rate (volume loss or wear track depth)
Microstructural analysis (e.g., SEM/EDS) to verify the formation of lubricious oxide tribofilm
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the boron-doped alloy does not consistently exhibit a statistically significant reduction in friction coefficient and wear rate compared to the undoped baseline across the tested temperatures (specifically around and above 704 °C), or if the lubricious oxide film does not form under the prescribed conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.
